feature: Webhook server endpoints (POST /ingest, GET /healthz|/dashboard|/report|/compliance) with X-DLE-Token auth, containerized via Docker
source: governance/server.py:_GovHandler.do_POST (lines 88-118), do_GET (lines 70-86), _auth_ok (lines 45-49), make_server (lines 121-125), run (lines 128-141); reference-impl/Dockerfile; governance/DEPLOY.md
user_story: As a platform operator, I want to self-host a dependency-light webhook that any agent's or human's CI can POST diffs to, gated by a shared-token header and deployable as a single Docker container, so that I can centralize governance ingestion behind TLS without standing up heavy infrastructure.
expected_behavior: A stdlib-only ThreadingHTTPServer (http.server, no third-party deps) serves: POST /ingest accepting JSON {org, repo, diff, author?, agent?, sha?}  -  it enforces a 5 MB body cap (MAX_BODY, 413 on overflow), 400s on invalid JSON or any missing required field among (org, repo, diff), then calls ingest_change with Attribution(author or 'unknown', agent or 'human') and returns 200 with {change_id, n_findings, chain_seq, files, findings:[{check_id, severity, file, line, framework}]}. GET /healthz returns {'ok': true, 'service': 'dle-govern'}; GET /dashboard|/report|/compliance require ?org= (400 if absent) and return HTML / text/plain via render_dashboard / org_report / compliance_report respectively; unknown paths return 404. Auth: _auth_ok is OFF when no token is configured; if DLE_GOV_TOKEN (passed as cfg['token']) is set, EVERY GET and POST must send a matching X-DLE-Token header or receive 401 before any work is done. make_server(db, token, host, port) builds (port=0 picks an ephemeral port for tests); run() reads DLE_GOV_HOST/PORT/TOKEN from env and serves forever. The Dockerfile (python:3.12-slim) pip-installs the package, sets DLE_GOV_DB=/data/governance.db on a VOLUME, binds DLE_GOV_HOST=0.0.0.0 DLE_GOV_PORT=8765, EXPOSEs 8765, and runs `python -m dual_log_engine.governance.server`; DEPLOY.md instructs operators to set DLE_GOV_TOKEN and terminate TLS in front (the server speaks plain HTTP). Hardening (all tested in tests/test_governance_server.py): auth uses a constant-time hmac.compare_digest token comparison (server.py:64); the Server header is hardened (server_version='dle-govern', sys_version='' - no Python-build banner); the POST validation ladder is: bad/negative Content-Length -> 400, body over 5MB -> 413, invalid JSON -> 400, non-dict JSON body -> 400, missing org/repo/diff -> 400, non-string org/repo/diff -> 400 'fields must be strings', blank/zero-width org or repo -> 400 (via _blank, matching the store's _tenant_key condition), ingest ValueError -> 400, any other exception -> 500 with no traceback leaked; GET applies the same blank-org 400 / ValueError 400 / 500-no-trace fallback.
edge_cases: DLE_GOV_TOKEN unset -> auth OFF: every request is accepted (run() banner prints 'auth OFF'); intended for local use only, and DEPLOY.md warns to set the token and front it with TLS in production. || POST body over 5 MB returns 413 'payload too large' before parsing; malformed JSON or missing org/repo/diff returns 400 with an explicit message. || Single-writer assumption (SQLite WAL only)  -  pointing two server instances at the same DB file is unsupported per DEPLOY.md; the audit DB must live on the persisted /data volume so container restarts don't lose the trail.
notes: Endpoints reuse the exact CLI render functions (render_dashboard, org_report, compliance_report, ingest_change), so webhook output matches CLI output for the same store. Auth check runs first in both do_GET and do_POST, so unauthorized callers can't even reach the org/field validation. log_message is silenced by default. Cross-ref SEC-9 (webhook input validation + Server-banner hardening).

feature: O(1) trace capture on the hot path
user_story: As a developer, I want every tool invocation recorded with a single fast write so that capturing my agent's activity never slows down or blocks my coding session.
expected_behavior: MemoryEngine.capture(tenant_id, repo_id, agent_run_id, text, trace_id=None) performs exactly one indexed INSERT into the episodic table via store.add_trace (no graph load, no LLM, no full rewrite). It auto-generates a trace_id of f'{agent_run_id}-{time.time_ns()}' when none is passed, stamps ts=time.time(), commits, and returns {'buffered': <int>} where the count comes from store.buffer_count(tenant_id, repo_id) scoped by (tenant_id, repo_id). Distillation is deliberately NOT on this path.
edge_cases: Two captures within the same agent_run_id in the same nanosecond are theoretically possible but time_ns() resolution makes collisions extremely unlikely; trace_id is not a uniqueness-enforced column (episodic PK is the autoincrement id), so even a duplicate trace_id inserts a distinct row rather than raising. || Empty text is still inserted (text column is NOT NULL but '' is allowed), so a no-op tool call still increments the buffer count. || Concurrent captures from hooks + MCP + daemon share the same WAL .db file; busy_timeout=5000 absorbs lock contention rather than failing.
notes: Hot path is intentionally one indexed write; heavy distillation work is pushed off this path to the daemon.

feature: Background distillation of overdue traces (distill_due)
source: engine.py:MemoryEngine.distill_due (lines 97-109) and MemoryEngine._distill (lines 84-95); store.py:SqliteStore.due_traces (lines 194-204) and groups_with_traces (lines 212-214)
user_story: As a platform operator, I want the daemon to sweep overdue episodic traces into the durable graph on each tick so that the raw buffer stays small and the permanent record builds up without operator intervention.
expected_behavior: distill_due(tenant_id=None, repo_id=None) is the daemon's per-tick job. With both ids it processes just [(tenant_id, repo_id)]; otherwise it enumerates store.groups_with_traces() (DISTINCT tenant_id, repo_id over episodic). For each group it calls store.due_traces(t, r, max_traces, max_age_seconds) which returns traces older than (now - max_age_seconds) OR beyond the most-recent max_traces (default 20 / 48h). Non-empty due sets are passed to _distill, which wraps rows as EpisodicTrace, calls worker.distill, then store.delete_traces([t['id']...]) to remove the raw rows, then await refresh_cache. Returns {'groups': <count touched>, 'distilled': <sum of len(entities)+len(relations)>}.
edge_cases: No groups with traces -> loops zero times, returns {'groups': 0, 'distilled': 0}. || A group whose traces are all within the recency/age window has due=[] and is skipped (touched not incremented), so steady low-volume repos never distill until they cross a threshold. || If distillation yields zero entities/relations, delete_traces still runs (raw rows removed) so traces are not re-distilled forever; 'distilled' stays 0 for that group.
notes: _distill deletes raw rows AFTER worker.distill succeeds and always refreshes the cache.

feature: Force-distill the entire buffer (flush)
user_story: As a developer, I want to force the whole remaining buffer for my repo to be distilled at session end so that nothing I just did is lost if no daemon is running.
expected_behavior: flush(tenant_id, repo_id) reads store.group_traces(tenant_id, repo_id)  -  the group's ENTIRE current buffer ordered by (ts ASC, id ASC), ignoring the recency/age thresholds used by distill_due  -  and passes all of it to _distill. _distill wraps traces, calls worker.distill, deletes the raw rows, and refreshes the cache. Returns {'flushed': len(traces), 'distilled': <entities+relations count>}. This is the session-end fallback (wired to the Stop hook).
edge_cases: Empty buffer -> group_traces returns [], _distill short-circuits to 0 (the 'if not traces: return 0' guard), result is {'flushed': 0, 'distilled': 0} and no cache refresh-bearing distill runs. || Called concurrently with the daemon distilling the same group, the second deletion of already-removed ids is harmless (delete_traces is idempotent by id). || Flush distills traces that are still 'recent' (would not yet be due), intentionally promoting fresh activity at session boundary.
notes: Differs from distill_due by ignoring thresholds  -  it always takes the full buffer.

feature: Dual-level RAG query (LOW / HIGH / HYBRID)
user_story: As an auditor/regulator, I want to retrieve a repo's distilled memory at a chosen abstraction tier so that I can inspect either pinpoint operational findings (LOW), systemic principles (HIGH), or both (HYBRID).
expected_behavior: MemoryEngine.query(tenant_id, repo_id, query, mode='HYBRID') delegates to dual_level_rag_query, which validates mode against {'LOW','HIGH','HYBRID'} (raises ValueError on anything else) and maps it via _MODE_TO_LEVEL: 'LOW'->level 'LOW', 'HIGH'->level 'HIGH', 'HYBRID'->None (both tiers). It calls store.fetch(tenant_id, repo_id, level)  -  an indexed predicate filter over (tenant_id, repo_id, level) returning only matching rows  -  and returns a CompiledContext(mode, query, tenant_id, repo_id, entities, relations). CompiledContext.to_prompt() renders an '# Retrieved memory context' block with '## Entities' bullets ([level] name (type): description) and '## Relations' bullets ([level] (Nx) source -rel-> target: description); .token_estimate runs estimate_tokens over that render.
edge_cases: Unknown mode (e.g. 'MEDIUM') raises ValueError('unknown mode ...; expected LOW, HIGH, or HYBRID') before touching the store. || A tenant/repo with no rows returns a CompiledContext with empty entities/relations; to_prompt() still emits the header/section scaffolding but no '- ' bullets (used downstream as the 'no content' signal). || Tenant/repo isolation is enforced in SQL  -  fetch never returns another tenant's rows even though the table is shared.
notes: async because this is the seam where a real embedding-retrieval step would slot in; HYBRID is level=None (no level filter).

feature: Pre-rendered cached context for fast injection
source: engine.py:MemoryEngine.cached_context (lines 130-132) and refresh_cache (lines 117-121) and _CACHE_QUERY/_CACHED_MODES (lines 35-36); store.py:SqliteStore.get_cache (lines 225-229) and set_cache (lines 218-223)
user_story: As a developer, I want injected memory context to be served from a pre-rendered cache so that adding repo memory to my prompt is a single fast SELECT instead of a live graph traversal.
expected_behavior: cached_context(tenant_id, repo_id, mode='HIGH') returns store.get_cache(...)  -  one SELECT of cache.payload keyed by (tenant_id, repo_id, mode), or None if cold. The daemon/_distill keep it warm via refresh_cache(tenant_id, repo_id), which iterates _CACHED_MODES = ('HIGH','HYBRID'), runs dual_level_rag_query with the natural-language label from _CACHE_QUERY ('durable guidelines and recurring risks' for HIGH, 'relevant prior context' for HYBRID), and store.set_cache(...) the ctx.to_prompt() string (upsert on conflict, stamping updated=time.time()). Injection hooks read this; only HIGH and HYBRID are pre-rendered (LOW is not cached).
edge_cases: Cold cache (no refresh has run yet) -> cached_context returns None; the SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit hooks fall back to a live engine.query. || Requesting mode='LOW' from cached_context returns None because refresh_cache only populates HIGH and HYBRID. || set_cache upsert overwrites prior payload for the same (tenant,repo,mode); a refresh after distillation always reflects the latest graph state.
notes: Cache is the read-time decoupling from graph traversal; refresh happens after every _distill.

feature: Eviction by count and age thresholds (last 20 / 48h)
user_story: As a compliance officer, I want raw operational traces to expire on a bounded last-20-or-48-hours policy so that short-lived sensitive telemetry does not accumulate indefinitely while durable distilled insight persists.
expected_behavior: Two grounded surfaces implement the same threshold. (1) EpisodicLogStore (in-memory path): _evict applies the age window first (drop ts < now - max_age_seconds via injectable now_fn) then the count cap (keep the most-recent max_traces in arrival order, evict overflow), returning aged_out + overflow; append fires the on_evict callback for evicted traces. Defaults are DEFAULT_MAX_TRACES=20 and DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_SECONDS=48*3600. (2) SqliteStore.due_traces (the on-disk path the daemon uses) computes cutoff = now - max_age_seconds and keep_recent_ids = the last max_traces by (ts ASC,id ASC), returning every trace whose ts < cutoff OR whose id is not in keep_recent_ids  -  i.e. older than the window OR beyond the recent cap, whichever is tighter. Eviction is per (tenant_id, repo_id) group.
edge_cases: max_traces=0 disables the recency keep-set (keep_recent_ids = empty set), so due_traces marks everything past the age cutoff as due (and nothing is kept by count). || now is injectable (now_fn / due_traces' now param) for deterministic age-window testing without sleeping. || A burst that exceeds max_traces evicts the oldest overflow immediately on append even if all traces are within the 48h window (count cap is the tighter constraint).
notes: Doctrine's sunset asymmetry: raw episodic logs expire, distilled graph persists. Per-group isolation.

feature: Pluggable LLM distillation clients (Mock / Anthropic / Headroom) + llm_from_env
source: clients.py:MockLLMClient (lines 145-172), AnthropicLLMClient (lines 222-274), HeadroomLLMClient (lines 277-298), LLMClient Protocol (lines 55-60); engine.py:llm_from_env (lines 39-45)
user_story: As a platform operator, I want distillation to run against a deterministic in-process mock by default and swap to a real model (optionally compressed) purely via environment variables so that the engine compiles and self-checks with no network or API key, yet upgrades to Opus-grade distillation in production without code changes.

MockLLMClient is deterministic and in-process: _batch_from_prompt splits on 'Raw Telemetry Corpus:', then _default_extract derives a stable dual-level graph (LOW: COMPONENT/ERROR_TYPE entities, CAUSES/RESOLVES edges; HIGH: one PRINCIPLE+SUBSYSTEM pair joined by DEPENDS_ON), and usage is filled by estimate_tokens (~4 chars/token). feature: Background distillation daemon (dle-serve)
user_story: As a platform operator, I want a resident daemon that polls the shared store and distils overdue traces on a fixed interval so that the graph and injection cache stay fresh without ever touching the agents' hot path.
expected_behavior: dle-serve (python -m dual_log_engine.daemon / console script run()) builds a MemoryEngine(root=args.root) and runs asyncio _loop. Each tick awaits engine.distill_due() (all groups), prints a stderr line when result['distilled'] is non-zero, then awaits asyncio.sleep(interval). It is fail-soft: a per-tick exception is caught, logged to stderr as '[dle-serve] tick error: <Type>: <msg>', and the loop continues. main() parses --root (default $DLE_MEMORY_DIR or '.memory') and --interval (default $DLE_INTERVAL or 3.0 seconds), prints a startup banner including the resolved llm class name, and wraps asyncio.run with a KeyboardInterrupt handler that prints '[dle-serve] stopped' on Ctrl-C.
edge_cases: A transient distill failure (e.g. store locked, LLM import error) is caught per-tick so one bad tick never kills the daemon. || interval can be sub-second (float); a very small interval increases poll pressure on the shared WAL db (busy_timeout absorbs contention). || Multiple daemons on the same .memory dir would double-distill; the design assumes a single resident process per store (SQLite is also the IPC).
notes: Selects backend from env via the engine's llm_from_env; DLE_LLM/DLE_HEADROOM honored through MemoryEngine. Behavior now directly proven: _loop awaits engine.distill_due exactly once per tick, and a RuntimeError raised inside a tick is caught + logged '[dle-serve] tick error' with the loop continuing.
